sections.text: He who is spiritual, who is pure, who has overcome his senses and his personal self, who has realised his highest Self as the Self of all, such a one, even though he acts, is not bound by his acts.
Though the saint sees, hears, touches, smells, eats, moves, sleeps and breathes, yet he knows the Truth, and he knows that it is not he who acts.
Though he talks, though he gives and receives, though he opens his eyes and shuts them, he still knows that his senses are merely disporting themselves among the objects of perception.

We had been discussing chapter five, Karma Sannyasa Yoga, Yoga of True Renunciation. So the chapter opens with Arjunas question, which one is better? You had been praising Sannyasa. At the same time you are asking me to engage in action.
Both are reaching the same goal. Whether you start with Karma Yoga or a Sannyasa, it will take you to the goal which you are striving all your life, that is finding a permanent bliss. Right now, it seems my life is filled with agitations and unhappiness.
No matter how hard I try, I cant get out of agitations. Even when I think Im doing something with good intentions, it creates agitations. As the Rolling Stones say, the road to hell is paved with good intentions.
We do think we are doing it with good intentions. We end up in a very uneasy situation. So how do I get out of it? One side, I think if I continue working harder and harder, Ill get to the point where there will be bliss.
Thats our retirement plan, isnt it? I want to work hard and work hard so I can get to a blissful retirement. Or say, Im so tired of this agitations and unhappiness, I should give up everything and not get involved in anything. Thats typically what we go through in our life at various stages of our life.
And thats basically Arjunas question. Bhagavan said no -- intelligently engaging yourself in either Karma or renouncing Karma will get you the same goal. However, for you, Karma Yoga is clearly better.
You are not at a state to renounce actions. I can only renounce something which I have. I cant renounce and say I have given up Hanover County.
I dont own Hanover County. I cant renounce Hanover county. Or I give Hanover county donation to Chinmaya Mission cant happen.
I have to have something to renounce. So if I have worked very hard in the field of my actions, then only I can retire from actions. If I never engage myself into actions, there is nothing to retire from.
The man who never worked in his life -- how can he retire? If youre not working Monday through Friday, there is no weekend. All seven days are weekend for you. So Bhagavan says the first thing is you have to engage yourself in actions.
You start with Karma Yoga, apply yourself into actions. And you start out your actions in life first with desire-prompted actions: I want to achieve this, I want to accomplish this, I want to get this -- and that will get me to happiness. Then he realized that thats not getting me anywhere.
Then started desire less actions. Bill Gates obviously started out with a lot of desires, built the biggest company, want to put PC on every home and build the largest company. And he did whatever is stuck to make the Microsoft the biggest company.
Now what hes doing is desireless actions. Hes giving up all the money he has earned. Hes engaging himself actively into his foundation to better peoples lives.
So I start out to get happiness through my desire-prompted actions. Then I graduate from desire-prompted actions to desireless actions. From desireless actions only can I graduate to agency-less action -- giving up the sense of I am the doer. Moving from selfish action to selfless action is a journey, and Karma Yoga is the means to achieve that.
So Bhagavan said that only the people who do not understand this journey will think that Karma Yoga is different from Sannyasa, or that Gnana Yoga is different from Karma Yoga. But one who establishes himself in one will get the result of both. Once I establish myself in Karma Yoga, my mind and intellect will purify and I will achieve that bliss.
Likewise, when I realize that Im not this limited being, that I am not the doer, then Ill achieve the same bliss. So Yat Sankhe Praapvyate Sthanam Tad Yogi API gamma te -- whatever is reached by the knowledge that I am not this limited being can also be achieved by performing Karma Yoga. So the one who sees that this is the same path leading to the same goal -- Yapasyati Sapashyati -- such a person realizes what the true destination is.
What is the true journey? Sanya Sastamaha Baha Dukham Aptama Yogatah. If I start renouncing things before achieving things, its very painful. I havent even gained anything -- how can I renounce anything? So first step to make myself worthy of giving up.
If I start giving up without achieving anything, I want to make a Donation of a million dollar. But I have only hundred thousand dollars in my bank. Its going to give me more pain.
If I achieve the level well, I can start giving up. Bill Gates could not have given up his money before Microsoft was built, right? So for one who wants to renounce before achieving anything, its very painful. Therefore, dont start thinking about giving up actions before you accomplish actions. Yoga Yukta, Munihi Brahman Achiranadhi Gacha Diprama.
Once you establish yourself in Karma Yoga -- which is selfless action, Niskama Karma -- moving from desire-prompted action to desireless action, it is very easy to give up after that. Then Sannyasa comes very naturally to us. See, therefore, in the Varnashrama system, you start with Brahmacharya, which is the life of a student.
Then Grihasthashram -- you have to engage yourself in activity, achieve things, produce things, do whatever it is to support society, your family, your community. Then Vanaprastham -- gradually retreat from all activity. Not suddenly, but gradually start giving up the powers to your juniors, your sons, whoever you consider.
And then Sannyasa -- you have already taken yourself out of action to a point where its very easy to exit. So you see, once you establish yourself in desireless actions, it is very easy to achieve that peace which you are looking for. Yoga Yukto Visuddhatma, Vijitatma Jitendriyaha, Sarva Bhuttma Bhutatma Kurvanapi Na Lipyate. Once I establish myself in desireless action and I want to take Sannyasa, that Sannyasa does not mean that I will not be acting in this world.
Outside, Ill be working in the world. But now the actions dont bind me. Yoga Yukta -- once one has established himself in Karma Yoga and the art of action. When I was learning music, obviously its so painful to do the Sa-Ra-Ga-Ma, the Sargam.
Once you establish in that, its very easy. So once you master anything, its very easy to perform that action. So to perform these actions in a right way, Bhagavan said is without desire.
You perform the same action without desires. Right now it is very difficult for me. Because everything is prompted by my desire.
I want to achieve this. So all this is creating agitations. Once Im out of agitations then it is very easy for me to give up.
So these are the qualifications Yoga Yuktah Once we established in how to perform actions. Visuddhaatma Vasudhatma. Your internal instrument is purified.
Mind and intellect is now purified. So it sees things as they are. And we are not polluted by my desires.
Right now the reality is colored by my desire. If the market is going up, we are all very happy. And the interest rates are at zero level.
Great for a businessman. But the guy who is retired and relying on investment income -- he is suffering with a 0% interest rate for so long. For a person surviving on investment income, 0% interest is a disaster.
For a person borrowing money to leverage his business, thats great. Theres never been a better time in this country than the last few years. So its all colored by my desire.
But the one who is not involved in both, he sees that as a normal occurring. This is how the world works and theres nothing to rejoice or regret about it. Vijay Tatma who has a control over his self in this case is ego.
Who has a control over his ego. He knows that these things are happening. Im just doing my part.
Jit Indriyaha -- one who has control over the senses. Indriyas are there for a purpose and they have their own reasons to be there. And I have control over what I see, what I hear, what I touch, what I taste.
I have control over it, not my senses. Sarva Bhuttma Bhuttatma -- now this is the real test of a Sannyasi. Once he starts seeing that the self in me is the self in all beings.
Myself and yourself and his self or herself are not various selves. One self manifesting as me, you, he, she, it. When that reason comes, Bhagavan says Kurvan API na lipya dhai.
He can do whatever he wants in this world but not affected by it. We are affected by our actions because we think Ive done good, that means Im going to get something out of it. Ive done bad, Im going to get punished by it.
All these things are because of my desires. But once I have transcended the desires -- see, when two children are playing and both are your children, who wins and who loses is not a problem. Serena Williams and Venus Williams -- at one time they were both in a Wimbledon final.
To their father, what does it matter which daughter is going to win? Guaranteed, he is happy either way -- otherwise he is jumping up and down in his chair. Whether his daughter is going to win or not, if I start seeing myself in everything, then whoever is winning or losing is all me winning and me losing. Therefore, Bhagavan always says, you are not suffering alone -- Im suffering with you.
When I suffer, he suffers at the same time. You know, different Puranas say that somebody did this or Bhagavan had the pain. Its symbolic.
But if I pervade everywhere in my dream, even the one who is suffering and one who is enjoying, both are me. So Bhagavan said, when I start seeing that Kurvanna pina Lipyade, then whatever I do is not affecting me. So the following three verses say the attitude of a person who has achieved that level of accomplishment and seeing things as one.
How that Sanyasi so is now a realized person. He has seen that the one self pervades everywhere and I am no different than it. His attitude will be Naiva kinship, Karomi Ithi, Yuktah, manyya tattvavit.
Here is the qualification or the description of a self-realized master -- Tattvavit -- who knows in essence what the reality is all about. There is no plurality as we see it. The perception of plurality is because I have confined myself to this limited identification.
I am one person when I identify this body as me. But when I represent a family or a company -- when I say Im from Google -- I represent Google. The entire Google pervades in me.
The whole power of that company I exude when I say I am from Google. I remember I used to work for large companies. So when I go to Austria or someplace, Im not Rajan Bart.
Im representing wzmh, one of the largest companies. When I take out my card and say Im Rajan Bart, wzmh. Im not presenting my qualifications -- Im presenting the qualifications of my company.
Then I left the company, started NBJ architecture with four people. Now I have to say I am who I am. It changes your perception when you expand your identification.
So one who has expanded his identification to the entire universe -- for him, Naiva kinchit karomi, I am not doing anything.

These three verses paint a remarkable portrait of the liberated soul in action. Verse 7 describes one who has realized his highest Self as the Self of all - and crucially, even though he acts, is not bound by his acts. Verses 8 and 9 then enumerate the full range of human activities - seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, moving, sleeping, breathing, talking, giving, receiving, even opening and closing the eyes - and declare that the wise one knows it is not he who acts. This is not philosophical theory but a lived experience: the recognition that his senses are merely disporting themselves among the objects of perception.
Practice this contemplation today: As you go through your activities, periodically pause and observe. Who is seeing? Who is hearing? Notice that the eyes see automatically, the ears hear automatically - you, the awareness behind it all, are simply witnessing. When eating lunch, notice that taste happens, chewing happens, swallowing happens. Can you locate the doer? This is the attitude of the tattvavit, the knower of Truth mentioned in verse 8. The goal is not to become passive or disconnected, but to recognize your true position as the unchanging witness while the body-mind instrument continues its natural functions. Even now, as you read these words, who is reading? Abide as that which knows.
